messages.subject: Re: Neagtive or greater than 1 values of mean probability of identity by state (IBS) - gl.grm function
parts:
Hi Adrian,

The method used to calculate the Genomic Relationship Matrix (GRM) involves centering the allele content for each locus using allele frequencies across all individuals in your dataset. This means that if your dataset has genetic structure (i.e., contains different populations), the off-diagonal values in the GRM can be less than zero or greater than one. For example, see Figure 1 in Endelman, J. B. , Jannink, J.-L. (2012). Shrinkage estimation of the realized relationship matrix. G3: Genes, Genomics, Genetics 2, 1405.

Values greater than one indicate a higher-than-expected genetic similarity between individuals—in other words, these individuals share more alleles identical by state than the average in the population. Conversely, values less than zero suggest that individuals are less related than the average pair in the population.

I recommend starting with a threshold of 0.5 when interpreting the GRM. After applying this threshold, compare the results with those from the gl.report.replicates function. This comparison will help you adjust the threshold accordingly.

Cheers,
Luis

parts:
Hi Adrian,

I added the option of changing the shape of the nodes in gl.grm.netwrok.

Please give it a go using after installing the developing version of dartR.base as below.

Cheers,
Luis 

devtools::install_github("green-striped-gecko/dartR.captive@dev")
library(dartRverse)
DART_SNP <- platypus.gl
shp <- gl.select.shapes(select = c(19, 19, 18, 18, 15, 15, 25, 17))
col <-
  gl.select.colors(
    library = 'brewer',
    palette = 'Paired',
    ncolors = 12,
    select = c(1, 2, 7, 8, 3, 4, 12, 5)
  )
col2 <-
  gl.select.colors(library = 'gr.hcl',
                   palette = 'Viridis',
                   ncolors = 9)

GRM <- gl.grm(DART_SNP)
NETWORK_Clones <- gl.grm.network(

GRM,
  DART_SNP,
  method = "kk",
  node.size = 10,
  node.label = T,
  node.label.size = 4,
  node.label.color = "black",

node.shape = shp,
  link.size = 3,
  relatedness_factor = 0.15,

title = NULL,
  palette_discrete = col,

link.color = col2,
  verbose = 3
)

Hi Adrian,

The method used to calculate the Genomic Relationship Matrix (GRM) involves centering the allele content for each locus using allele frequencies across all individuals in your dataset. This means that if your dataset has genetic structure (i.e., contains different populations), the off-diagonal values in the GRM can be less than zero or greater than one. For example, see Figure 1 in Endelman, J. B. , Jannink, J.-L. (2012). Shrinkage estimation of the realized relationship matrix. G3: Genes, Genomics, Genetics 2, 1405.

Values greater than one indicate a higher-than-expected genetic similarity between individuals—in other words, these individuals share more alleles identical by state than the average in the population. Conversely, values less than zero suggest that individuals are less related than the average pair in the population.

I recommend starting with a threshold of 0.5 when interpreting the GRM. After applying this threshold, compare the results with those from the gl.report.replicates function. This comparison will help you adjust the threshold accordingly.

Cheers,
Luis
